prose.summary: Your steel building structures qualify for preferential customs duty under the India-UAE CEPA because the product meets the required rule of origin. By claiming the CEPA rate, you can reduce the basic customs duty in India to 0%, resulting in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. Please refer to the claim checklist below for the next steps.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 73089090 for 'Other structures of iron or steel', with high confidence. You should confirm this tariff code with Indian customs or a customs broker prior to shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate for this tariff line is an effective rate of 10% (tariff rate 15%), whereas the CEPA rate is 0%. Claiming this trade agreement preference offers an estimated duty saving of 10000.00 AED on your shipment.
prose.origin: To qualify, the product must meet a rule of origin requiring a Change in Tariff Subheading (CTSH, meaning each non-originating material comes from a different 6-digit tariff subheading than the finished good) and a regional Value Addition (VA) of at least 40%. The product satisfies these criteria because final manufacture occurs in the UAE, the work completed goes beyond minimal operations, all 2 non-originating inputs satisfy the CTSH requirement outside subheading 730890, and the value addition reaches 45.0% on an FOB basis (the price loaded on board at the UAE port).

notes.text: The tariff schedule prints 15%, but an exemption notification lowers the duty actually charged to 10%; the effective rate is used.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
